subject: Exec: line-of-sight OKR sync & budget launch
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-27T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Exec: line-of-sight OKR sync & budget launch

Team —

Kicking off a condensed annual planning thread so we have clear line-of-sight into OKRs, budget impacts, and QBR preparation. High-level asks and timeline below; please read and reply with your initial signals by EOD Friday (Apr 2).

Objectives
- Capture org-level OKR deltas and the budget implications for FY27 (heads, run-rate, capital).
- Produce 1-page scenario packs (Base / Conservative / Upside) with clear triggers for each band.
- Lock QBR presentation owners and a runbook for the exec review.

Initial timeline (proposed)
- Apr 2: Signals due (one-line: commit level + top risk)
- Apr 6: One-pagers + budget template return
- Apr 12–16: Exec QBR run-throughs and dry-runs

Action items / owners
- Vivek: own scenario bands & capacity model (I'll need per-region throughput assumptions).
- Laura: consolidate cross-functional asks and services impacts.
- Stephanie: lead QBR narrative and slide template.
- Aditya: surface hiring/comp plans and any critical headcount asks.
- Jonas: run the prep schedule and invite cadence.

Attachments: planning_template_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_planning_timeline

Please flag any blockers — procurement, compliance, or critical vendor timelines that would force a reprioritization.

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Strategy & Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-27T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exec: line-of-sight OKR sync & budget launch

Thanks — I’ll take the scenario bands and capacity model. Quick notes:
- I’ll baseline on current dedicated + hosted forecasts and then model a conservative case that assumes 20% slower GTM growth through Q3.
- We need to call out GPU procurement lead times (6–8 weeks for certain SKUs) as a procurement constraint in the Conservative band. I’ll attach an updated capacity worksheet.

Attaching: capacity_model_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Agree with the plan — two asks from Product/Hiring lens:
1) Headcount data: we can produce the headcount plan but will need until Apr 8 to finalize offers and comp impacts (several candidates in final loop). Can we move the "one-pager + budget template return" from Apr 6 to Apr 8 for orgs with hiring asks?
2) Ramp assumptions: will add a short table of expected ramp and calendarized hiring costs.

Attaching: headcount_assumptions.docx (document)

If procurement/contract timing is binding for a few customers we should mark those line items as immovable. Otherwise I support the timeline but want to be explicit about the hiring slip risk.

From: Maya Singh <finance@acme.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-30T16:50:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exec: line-of-sight OKR sync & budget launch

Irene / Marissa —

Thanks for the heads up. A couple of procurement items from Acme Finance so we can slot the PO and billing cadence into your timeline:
- We generally need a signed SOW + PO 30 days before the start of a paid engagement; can you confirm when Redwood expects to finalize SOW language for customers engaged in Q2–Q3?
- Our preferred cadence is net-30 monthly invoicing; if there are scope-based milestones we can support milestone billing but need early visibility.
- Do you have a sample SOW and the billing contact for procurement?

If it helps, I can jump on a quick 20-min call next week to align timelines.

Best,
Maya Singh
Head of Finance Operations
Acme Corp

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Singh <finance@acme.com>
Date: 2026-03-31T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exec: line-of-sight OKR sync & budget launch — consolidated next steps

Thanks everyone — quick consolidation and final asks after the first round of replies:

Decisions / updated timeline
- Signals due: Apr 2 still stands (one-line: commit level + top risk).
- One-pagers + templates: Apr 6 for most orgs; Aditya/Prod organizations with active hiring may submit by Apr 8 (per Aditya).
- Exec QBR run-throughs: schedule dry-runs Apr 13–15; full Exec review week of Apr 19. Jonas will send invites.

Procurement note
- Maya: thanks for the detail. Marissa will coordinate a sample SOW and provide the billing contact. For our planning, mark critical customers that require signed SOWs by Apr 1 so we can prioritize procurement.

Deliverables checklist
- 1-pager scenario pack (Base / Conservative / Upside) — owner (Vivek) to include capacity constraints.
- Budget template (completed) — use planning_template_v1.xlsx.
- Hiring table + ramp (Aditya) — headcount_assumptions.docx used as reference.
- QBR narrative deck (Stephanie) — will circulate slide template by Apr 5.

Attachments: final_launch_plan_v1.pdf (pdf)
DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/launch?doc=RDW-PLANNING-2026
HubSpot: HUBSPOT-OPP-2026-0043

Next steps
- Jonas: send recurring prep slot invites and solidify dry-run slots (Apr 13–15).
- All: drop signals into the shared Drive folder by Apr 2; Laura will consolidate and return a one-page executive summary before Apr 9.

If anything is blocking your ability to meet these dates (procurement, compliance, hiring), flag it in reply and tag Marissa for assistance.

Appreciate the quick alignment — this keeps the QBR focused and gives the executive team line-of-sight on downside options.

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Strategy & Ops
Redwood Inference
